method: Sequential runs under GNU time -v, same saved 123-rule argv, default eight workers and four-million syntax-node retention. TIMINGS and CACHE_STATS enabled; JOBS, AST_CACHE_NODES and MALLOC_ARENA_MAX unset. Baseline executable archived before edits. Findings compared as sorted unique complete tagged physical lines joined by LF, without a trailing LF or other normalization. Host activity is uncontrolled. Cache counters describe retained payloads at exit, not peak RSS; GNU time measures process RSS independently.

changes: One 128 MiB buffer-capacity LRU for masked comments and lexer-cleaned source; active consumers hold independent strong references. Weak slots use Arc<String> so expired slots release text buffers.
Lazy boxed line indexes use u32 for files no larger than u32::MAX bytes, usize otherwise.
limits: This bounds retained derived-text buffers, not total RSS or live rule working sets. Source snapshots, syntax trees, compiler facts and cross-file indexes remain separate. Evicted views can be recomputed; elapsed time varies with scheduling and host load.
